chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from al-Ala' from Muhammad from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) said:

I said to him: 'Regarding the man who intends to perform night prayer (Qiyam al-Layl), if a night, two nights, or three nights pass without him praying, is it more beloved to you that he makes up the missed prayers, or that he hastens the Witr prayer at the beginning of the night?' He said, 'No, rather he makes up the missed prayers, even if it is thirty nights.'

key_terms.أَوَّلَ اللَّيْلِ: At the beginning of the night

ai.seo_question: What should one do if they miss night prayers for multiple nights?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the preference for making up missed voluntary night prayers (Qada) over performing Witr at the start of the night highlights the importance of preserving the specific spiritual discipline of night worship even after a lapse. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that consistency in the *method* of worship (night vigil) takes precedence over mere routine, ensuring the believer does not lose the unique merit of Qiyam al-Layl. It reflects the broader principle that voluntary acts, when missed, retain their distinct identity and should be recovered rather than replaced by other forms of devotion.
